m:stephan: The cathedral is open from 6am to 10pm (Sundays and holidays from 7am), but visitors can only tour the nave outside services. You can climb the south tower (every day 9am–7pm) or take the lift to the Pummerin bell (9am–8:30pm from April to December, 9am–5:30pm from January to March). The catacombs and towers have a separate ticket (prices on stephanskirche.at: not read).
m:hofburg: Sisi Museum and Imperial Apartments ticket: €20 (official website, via guides). From 6 October to 18 November 2026 the Sisi Museum section is closed and the ticket costs about 25% less (about €15): the Imperial Apartments stay open, from 10am to 4:30pm. The rest of the year 9am–5:30pm, last entry 4:30pm, every day. The Imperial Treasury costs €16 online, €18 at the desk. The Silver Collection has been closed indefinitely since 2023. From 19 November prices may change: check hofburg-wien.at.
m:schonbrunn: 2026 prices: «Imperial Tour» (Franz Joseph's apartments, 40 minutes) €28, «Palace Ticket» (the whole state section, 75 minutes) €38, Classic Pass with gardens €44; the park is free from 6:30am (prices and hours change with the seasons: from November the palace's winter hours weren't published on the pages I read, check schoenbrunn.at). A time slot is compulsory: book online. The palace Christmas market is open from 6 November 2026 to 6 January 2027.
m:belvedere: Open every day from 9am to 6pm; you need a ticket with an entry time (free to book online on the museum website). Upper Belvedere €23, Lower Belvedere €20, combined ticket €32 (from the museum website, undated prices). The garden is free. The Belvedere Christmas market is open from 20 November to 31 December 2026.
m:ring: Free to walk. You can only enter Parliament on a booked guided tour; the State Opera runs paid guided tours (times on the Opera website). In front of the City Hall from 13 November to 26 December there's the Christkindlmarkt, Vienna's most famous Christmas market.
m:museums: Open every day from 10am to 6pm, Thursdays until 9pm (museum website). Ticket €22 online, €24 at the desk. Since 8 September 2026 you need to book a time slot. Under-19s go free. The MuseumsQuartier is a courtyard open to all.
m:naschmarkt: The stalls are open Monday–Friday from 6am to 9pm and Saturday from 6am to 6pm; closed on Sundays (restaurants and bars 9am–9pm). On Saturdays there's the flea market. Monday and Tuesday are the least crowded days.
m:karls: The church can normally be visited Monday–Saturday 9am–6pm and Sunday from noon to 7pm (from guides, hours to be checked on karlskirche.at). Entry is paid, about €9–10 (price not read on the website).
m:prater: The Riesenrad is normally open every day from 9am to 11:45pm; the ticket costs €14.50 (price from the Vienna Tourism website, undated). The rides are open all year but many close in the cold. The Prater «Wintermarkt» usually opens in the second half of November.
m:hundert: The façade and the street are free to see; the house can't be visited inside. The «Hundertwasser Village» opposite is a touristy shop and café.
vd:kameel: A historic 1618 delicatessen with a buffet counter of small sandwiches and an Art Nouveau-ceilinged restaurant: little sandwiches with salmon, ham or cheese eaten standing or at the tables, with a glass of wine.
vp:kameel: Three sandwiches and a glass are about €10–14; a full breakfast €12–16 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:trzes: Vienna's open-sandwich chain: since 1902 it has served small sandwiches with spreads of egg, tuna, gherkin or horseradish, to eat standing with a small glass of beer. It was Kafka's favourite.
vp:trzes: A sandwich costs about €1.80–2.20; three make a snack (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:bitzinger: The sausage stand in front of the Albertina, behind the Opera: Käsekrainer, the cheese-filled sausage, and Bosna, with mustard and bread. The classic Viennese lunch break.
vp:bitzinger: A sausage with bread usually costs €6–8 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:gulasch: A place a short walk from St Stephen's with a menu devoted to goulash in many versions, with bread or dumplings: simple Viennese cooking at decent prices for the centre.
vp:gulasch: A goulash with bread or dumplings is around €12–16 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:landtmann: A historic 1873 café on the Ring, opposite the Burgtheater, once frequented by Freud: marble, tables covered in newspapers and a menu of Wiener Schnitzel, Apfelstrudel and Melange.
vp:landtmann: A coffee with a cake is around €10–13 and a dish of the day around €15–20 (menu not seen). Hours from the website, to be confirmed.
vd:museum: The café designed by Adolf Loos in 1899, sober and bright, a short walk from the Opera: Viennese breakfasts, cakes and simple dishes in airy rooms.
vp:museum: Breakfast around €10–14 and a dish around €13–18 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:sperl: One of Vienna's most authentic cafés, open since 1880 near the Naschmarkt: billiards, newspapers and an atmosphere frozen in the 20th century. Have a Melange or an Einspänner with Sachertorte.
vp:sperl: A coffee with a slice of cake is around €9–12 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:prueckel: A 1950s café on the Ring, opposite the Museum of Applied Arts: blue armchairs, newspapers and a menu of cakes and simple dishes.
vp:prueckel: A coffee with a cake is around €8–11 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
cd:albertina: Impressionists and works by Monet, Picasso and Klimt in the apartments of a Habsburg palace.
cd:leopold: The world's largest collection of Egon Schiele, plus Klimt and Viennese modernism.
cd:naturhist: The Venus of Willendorf, dinosaurs and a hall of minerals, opposite the Kunsthistorisches.
cd:staatsoper: The opera house seen from behind the scenes: auditorium, boxes and grand staircase.
cx:staatsoper: Tours run at fixed times and not when there's a rehearsal.
cd:stephansturm: 343 steps to the top of the tower, with views over the old town.
cd:kapuzinergruft: The crypt with the Habsburg tombs, including Sisi's.
cd:hausmusik: The museum of sound: interactive rooms where you compose, conduct and listen.
cd:hofreitschule: The Lipizzaner stallions training in the Hofburg's Baroque hall.
cx:hofreitschule: Morning training is on limited days and times: check the calendar.
cd:kunsthaus: The museum designed by Hundertwasser, with paintings and a building that breaks every rule.
cd:donauturm: The tower on the Danube, with an observation deck and a revolving restaurant.
cd:tiergarten: The world's oldest zoo, in Schönbrunn park: pandas and polar animals.
